fair_value.method: Blend of a pro forma (post-ASM, post-VAC, ~331M shares) sum-of-the-parts (~$9.5, 60%), a forward EV/sales cross-check on ~$700M pro forma 2027 revenue at 6x (~$9.8, 30%) and a haircut sell-side consensus target (~$14.5, 10%); pro forma 2027 net debt assumed ~$0.96B after the $718M VAC cash payment, OSC/Goldman loans and ~$300M growth capex.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Uranium segment EV $1.1B (~2.0-2.6M lb/yr at ~$80 realized vs $23-35/lb cost, ~$80-100M EBITDA x ~11-12x, plus resource optionality); REE platform (White Mesa Phase 1/2 + Vara Mada, company-stated combined NPV $3.7B) risked at ~35% = $1.3B; Donald JV stake $0.1B; ASM (Korean Metals Plant, Dubbo) $0.15B; VAC EV $1.2B (2025 adj. EBITDA $29M rising to ~$80M in 2027 incl. Sumter ramp toward $65-75M run-rate, x15); inventory/vanadium/isotopes/other $0.15B. Total EV ~$4.0B less pro forma net debt ~$0.96B (cash+securities ~$0.96B + $0.975B new OSC/GS loans - $0.718B VAC cash - ~$0.36B capex/burn; debt = $700M 0.75% converts (conv. $20.34, out of the money) + $725M OSC + $250M GS + $140M VAC net debt) = ~$3.1B / ~331M shares = ~$9.5.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue: consensus ~$262M standalone (stockanalysis/S&P) + ~$450M VAC (my estimate; VAC revenue not disclosed in sources, owler range $100-500M) = ~$710M; 6.0x EV/sales (premium to industrial magnet makers, discount to MP Materials-style strategic multiple given dilution and negative EPS) = EV ~$4.25B less net debt ~$0.96B = $3.3B / 331M shares = ~$9.9 (rounded down to $9.8 for execution risk).

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Sell-side consensus 12-month target $24.15 (8 analysts, range $16-$32.50) haircut 40% for historical optimism of targets on pre-revenue critical-minerals stories and the fact targets were largely set before the Aug-Sep drawdown.

bear.story: VAC closes into weak tape with heavy Ara share overhang (19.9% holder), OSC loan terms/timing slip or VAC closing delayed, US-China rare-earth thaw compresses the 'Western supply chain' premium, REE Phase 1 slips beyond 2028 and Vara Mada stalls on Madagascar politics; uranium drifts to $70s. Market values the company near a risked NAV of ~$6 and continued losses (EPS still negative) weigh.

base.story: VAC closes ~Q1 2027 as planned, uranium stays ~$85-95 with ~2M lb/yr output at ~$25-35/lb, Phase 1B/1C heavy REE construction on track for late-2027 Tb/Dy, Donald FID reached; sector sentiment remains mixed. Stock trades around a pro forma SOTP of ~$10 with high volatility.

bull.story: Renewed US-China rare-earth tension or new US price-floor/offtake support (MP-style DoD deal), Sumter magnet ramp and >$2B customer pipeline convert into signed contracts, uranium breaks above $100, Japanese/US customers qualify heavy REE; strategic multiple returns toward the $24 consensus target range and the 2025-26 highs ($27.90).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$6 the equity (~$2.0B pro forma) would be worth less than the uranium business plus the price just paid for VAC net of debt, which would most likely signal a fundamental problem: failed/renegotiated VAC financing (OSC $725M loan is only conditional), a liquidity squeeze from ~$1.8B of gross debt against a still loss-making P&L, a major REE project write-down (Vara Mada/Madagascar) or a sustained uranium price collapse, rather than ordinary 70-90% volatility.

VAC acquisition closing; issuance of 65.85M shares to Ara Partners (overhang)

key_uncertainties: Whether VAC closes on time and on the announced financing terms (OSC loan is conditional) and how much the 65.85M-share Ara stake weighs on the stock
VAC's actual revenue/EBITDA trajectory (2025 adj. EBITDA only $29M against a $2.04B EV) and Sumter ramp to $65-75M run-rate
Rare-earth policy premium: US-China thaw vs escalation, and NdPr/Tb/Dy prices
Uranium price path from ~$90/lb and 2027 production growth
Execution/timing of REE Phase 1B/1C ($104M) and Phase 2, Vara Mada permitting in Madagascar, Donald FID
Balance sheet: ~$1.8B pro forma gross debt vs ~$1B liquidity with ongoing operating losses; risk of further equity issuance
reasoning: Energy Fuels (UUUU) is a ~$2.9-3.0B market-cap uranium producer turning itself into a mine-to-magnet rare-earth platform. Evidence: Q2-2026 revenue $25.1M, EPS -$0.13 (miss, incl. $10.7M deal costs), uranium cost ~$23/lb, H1 production 1.7M lb, 2026 guidance maintained; uranium spot ~$90/lb in Sept 2026. Balance sheet at 6/30: ~$961M cash+securities, $700M 0.75% converts (conv. $20.34). ASM closed 8/28/2026 (small share issuance); VAC ($1.9B equity: $718M cash + 65.85M shares, plus $140M net debt, for a business with $29M 2025 EBITDA) expected to close early 2027, funded by a conditional $725M OSC loan + $250M Goldman loan. The stock fell from $16.12 at the VAC announcement to $11.35 (near the $10.69 52-week low, -59% from $27.90 high) on dilution/valuation concerns, the Q2 miss, rare-earth sector de-rating on US-China thaw hopes, and higher long rates. My pro forma SOTP (uranium ~$1.1B, risked REE ~$1.3B, VAC ~$1.2B, other ~$0.4B, less ~$0.96B net debt, 331M shares) gives ~$9.5; EV/sales cross-check ~$9.8; a heavily haircut consensus target ($24.15) gets 10% weight -> fair value ~$10.1, modestly below spot; the market still pays a strategic premium I only partly underwrite. Distribution: lognormal-like with median ~$10.2 and ~72% annualized log-vol (below the 89% trailing because the balance sheet and producing uranium business anchor value, but still far above the large-cap 25-35% base rate), giving P(>=11.35) ~0.44 and a fat right tail (P(>=28) ~7.5%) for a policy-driven rare-earth re-rating. Left tail trimmed slightly because ~$1B liquidity and a real uranium business make sub-$3 unlikely within 12 months. Scenario mean (~$11.6) is roughly consistent with the ladder. Research limits: no access to VAC revenue disclosure or the Sept 2026 Australian investor-day materials; Twelve Data estimates required a higher plan; option data deliberately not consulted.
